title: Explicit complete Saga/execution/runtime products and binding assemblies

saga_phase.description: v1 resource-typed command bindings must use the step participant's exact resource arg. No guessing address from first field, and no unsupported cross-resource parameter semantics.

saga_group.description: v1 groups are explicit serial numeric barriers: each group depends transitively on the previous numeric group. Steps within one group are concurrent and cannot reuse a participant. No implicit array-order join or dynamic DAG scheduler.

saga_trigger.description: Each trigger is an independent start mapping, not an inferred OR/AND/join. sourceRef resolves the owned command/event; source:<field> refs map every declared arg exactly. The named idempotency mapper derives stable transaction identity under Saga ID/version from durable business operation ID and rejects different args; no clock/random/generation/attempt identity.

saga_resilience.description: Bounded retry budgets retain the original operation identity. Retries require idempotency or reconciled nonexecution. totalTimeoutMs covers maxAttempts*(phaseTimeoutMs+queryTimeoutMs)+(maxAttempts-1)*backoffMs; expiry yields controlled recovery/unknown, not business rejection or automatic compensation.

saga_safety.description: All Prepare receipts must be confirmed before durably recording CommitDecision; only then Commit. AbortDecision is valid only before CommitDecision; reconcile unknown Prepare before compensating confirmed reservations. After CommitDecision never auto-compensate. Success requires every Commit confirmation. These are required host semantics, not observed runtime facts.

saga_admission.description: Static logical participant count and each concurrent barrier must fit the declared bounds. maxItemsPerChunk bounds each collection arg including nested collection cardinality; such args require durable-reference manifest. Runtime value conservation, arg inequality and manifest contents require host validation and are never certified here.

saga_product.title: Saga v1 contract-only IR, business declarations and technical bindings
saga_product.description: Only aggregate-owned commands (the public slice projection) and events resolve. Sessions are narrative, not proof of ownership. No runtime certification, code evaluation, implicit joins, dynamic participant expansion, numeric money or literal dataflow in v1. All-none steps are explicitly read-only. Step output refs are phase-qualified durable receipts; compensation may read only its own Prepare outputs. Digest is SHA-256 of stable JSON {schemaVersion,workshop,readiness,sagas}, excluding provenance/anchors.

execution_outcome.description: success/resolved must continue; business-rejection must stop or enter manual recovery; unknown-effect/infrastructure-failure must enter manual recovery. No retry, compensation, implicit default or arbitrary policy evaluation in v1. Writes must be returned on every continuing outcome, including resolved.

execution_recovery.description: The host must durably save every initial input before accepting a run. Recovery references must cover all initial inputs, not outputs produced later. Exact plan and codec compatibility are declarations, not a JVM ownership or journal verification.

execution_admission.description: Finite host admission/chunk limits; an emitter must wire them or reject generation. The ordered checkpoint window is exactly one. No unbounded streams or durable dynamic insertion in v1.

execution_stepExecution.description: Exactly one discriminator property: port, invokeSaga or awaitChildRun. An invocation is never a pure port, arbitrary expression, or runtime certificate; an awaited child run is never a pure port, implicit success, or dynamic insertion.

execution_transactionIdentity.description: Host derives transaction identity from Saga ID/version, pipeline ID (the enclosing pipeline.id), durable source token, exact stage ID, durable stage occurrence and each declared iteration/chunk token. All tokens must be typed reads of durable initial inputs; source is an ID, other tokens are IDs or bounded nonnegative integers in the Saga binding. No expressions, FQNs, clock, random, attempt or JVM generation. Missing optional tokens mean a single occurrence dimension, not inferred dynamic iteration.

execution_sagaResultMapping.description: Exact coverage of the five Saga results and step outcomes. Only succeeded maps to success/continue; rejected-before-effects and compensated map to business-rejection with stop/manual-recovery. recovery-required maps to infrastructure-failure/manual-recovery; outcome-unknown to unknown-effect/manual-recovery. Only continuing results publish writes, mapped from typed completion event payload fields. v1 has no resolved-policy-ref; compensation is never implicitly success or resolved.

execution_invokeSaga.description: Persist pinned ref, exact args/codec and derived identity as durable intent before requesting Saga start; replay reattaches using the same identity. Await a terminal confirmation before checkpointing success. RecoveryRequired and Unknown are controlled manual outcomes, never successful terminal completion. Contract declaration only.

execution_childResultMapping.description: Exact coverage of the five child-run results. Only succeeded maps to success/continue and publishes writes from the child's durable completed-manifest fields. child-rejected (StartRun refused with a reason other than already-in-state) maps to business-rejection/stop; child-failed (RunFailedEvt) maps to business-rejection/stop. recovery-required maps to infrastructure-failure/manual-recovery; outcome-unknown to unknown-effect/manual-recovery. A rejected re-attach (already in state) is not a result kind — the host treats it as already-attached and keeps observing. Compensation is never stage recovery.

execution_childRunIdentity.description: Host derives the child run identity from the parent operation key (a durable source token), the exact await step ID and a durable stage occurrence token, plus an optional chunk token. All tokens must be typed reads of durable initial inputs. No expressions, FQNs, clock, random, attempt or JVM generation. Re-attaching with the same identity is the only legal re-entry; different payload with the same identity is a conflict.

execution_awaitChildRun.description: Persist the derived child identity and exact payload as durable intent before requesting StartRun; replay reattaches using the same identity (a refusal saying the run is already in state means attached, not conflict). Observe the child's terminal state on its durable journal; a mirrored progress record is derived and never authoritative. RunFailedEvt pauses with recovery-required; it never auto-compensates the parent. Contract declaration only.

execution_invocationBinding.description: One adapter binding per invoked step; exact ref/runtime and args codec equality with the independently compiled Saga binding. Result codec version equals pinned args codec version. Type implementations agree exactly with Saga bindings; invoked Sagas in one pipeline must agree on shared nominal type contracts including referenced element/field bindings. Participant-resource mappings remain statically non-aliasing after args substitution. Runtime capabilities, participants, phase ports and completion mappers stay in sagaBindings, not duplicated here. Named adapters/mappers are never loaded or certified.

execution_childRunBinding.description: One child run binding per awaitChildRun step. The child plan is a separately compiled stages pipeline bound to monarch-persistence; the host derives the child persistence id from pidPrefix plus the derived run identity. The child's durable journal is the authoritative terminal-state source. Named mappers are never loaded or certified.

execution_idempotency.description: key is the name of an input slot (never source code). An external port requires keyed idempotency and a key whose reference is an initial input, stable across replay.

execution_port.description: External effects require durable-ack, stable keyed idempotency, and an explicit unknown-effect outcome. Every port must declare success and infrastructure-failure. The compiler checks coverage/equality, not behavior of the implementation.

execution_codec.description: compatibleVersions must include version. These are host codec declarations; they do not certify byte compatibility.

execution_canonicalEnvelope.description: Only the canonical envelope and pipeline identities are checked here. This does not replace validateTree or validate the rest of canonical. An execution property opts in, including a malformed/null declaration. Steps without a pipeline declaration may not carry execution.

execution_product.title: Truthsrc execution IR v1
execution_product.description: A compiled, contract-only execution model; not proof of runtime support. Input contracts are in $defs.execution, $defs.stepExecution and $defs.bindingDocument. Canonical narrative fields remain outside the execution contract. Reference grammar: input:<id> or step:<step-id>:<write-id>. Types are nominal IDs resolved by binding.types; no language expressions are accepted on the business surface. Optional binding.sagaBindings is an independently strict truthsrc.saga-binding/v1 document, required for invokeSaga; compileSagas validates all canonical.sagas when opted in. IR sagas contains each compiled definition/binding once, while pipeline binding.invocations declares adapters. No dynamic iteration, runtime execution, code generation or artifact certification.

$comment: Complete shape only; source reconstruction, runtime capability/pin and nominal dataflow checks remain mandatory.
